items.q: Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disease caused by a defect in:
items.exp: Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disease caused by a defect in α-galactosidase. (Book p784)

items.q: Match each Fabry feature with its description — 1) Angiokeratoma  2) Accumulation in vessels  3) Renal involvement … A) Heart, cerebrovascular and cornea verticillata  B) Appears in the 2nd decade  C) Asymptomatic microhaematuria + proteinuria, the earliest, with ESRD by the 4th–5th decade
items.exp: Fabry features: acroparesthesia; angiokeratoma (2nd decade); accumulation in vessels of heart, cerebrovascular system and cornea verticillata; renal — asymptomatic microhaematuria + proteinuria (earliest) with ESRD by the 4th–5th decade. (Book p784)

items.q: The earliest renal abnormality in Fabry disease is:
items.exp: Renal involvement in Fabry disease: asymptomatic microhaematuria + proteinuria is the earliest, culminating in ESRD by the 4th–5th decade. (Book p784)

items.q: In Fabry disease, ESRD develops by the:
items.exp: Renal feature of Fabry disease: asymptomatic microhaematuria + proteinuria (earliest) with ESRD by the 4th–5th decade. (Book p784)

items.q: Fill up: The skin lesion of Fabry disease shown in the figure is ______, appearing in the 2nd decade.
items.exp: Fabry disease produces angiokeratoma (in the 2nd decade), shown in the accompanying figure. (Book p784)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed as sites of vessel accumulation in Fabry disease. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Accumulation in vessels is described for heart, cerebrovascular system and cornea verticillata; the renal features are microhaematuria/proteinuria and podocyte vacuolation. (Book p784)

items.q: A 32-year-old man has acroparesthesia, angiokeratomas over the bathing-trunk area and proteinuria. Urine microscopy under polarised light shows lipid deposits. Which investigation matches Fabry disease?
opts: Urine — maltese cross deposits under polarised light; biopsy — vacuolation of podocytes
Urine — hexagonal cystine crystals; biopsy — glomerular crescents
Urine — calcium oxalate crystals; biopsy — calcium deposits
Urine — oval fat bodies only; biopsy — normal glomeruli
items.exp: Investigations in Fabry disease: urine shows maltese cross deposits under polarised light; renal biopsy shows vacuolation of podocytes. (Book p784)

items.q: Match each Fabry investigation with its finding — 1) Urine  2) Renal biopsy … A) Vacuolation of podocytes  B) Maltese cross deposits under polarised light
items.exp: Fabry disease: urine shows maltese cross deposits under polarised light; renal biopsy shows vacuolation of podocytes (figure 'Fabry's disease'). (Book p784)

items.q: Fill up: The lipid deposits in the urine of Fabry disease appear as ______ crosses under polarised light.
items.exp: Urine in Fabry disease: maltese cross deposits under polarised light, from lipid-laden cells. (Book p784)

items.q: A young man with Fabry disease has both renal and extrarenal disease. Which extrarenal symptom is listed first among his features?
items.exp: The features list of Fabry disease begins with acroparesthesia, then angiokeratoma (2nd decade), vessel accumulation in heart/cerebrovascular/cornea, and renal involvement. (Book p784)

items.q: Fabry disease is inherited in an X-linked manner and is a lysosomal storage disorder.
opts: True, but it is a peroxisomal disorder
items.exp: Fabry disease: X-linked lysosomal storage disease due to α-galactosidase defect. (Book p784)
